# **Product Requirements Document (PRD)**  
**Feature: Theme Scheduler**  
**Product:** Ledgerly – Note-Taking App  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** April 5, 2025  

---

## **1. Executive Summary**

Night-shift nurses use Ledgerly to read clinical notes between 2am and 6am. During these hours, users report significant eye strain due to the app’s manual light/dark toggle, which requires them to switch themes repeatedly and often in low-light environments. This leads to increased user fatigue and a rise in support tickets related to theme-related issues—currently averaging 12 tickets per week.

To address this, we are introducing a **Theme Scheduler** feature that automatically adjusts the app’s theme based on time-of-day schedules. The scheduler allows users to define two time-based theme schedules (e.g., "dark from 2am to 6am") and will automatically apply the appropriate theme during those windows. When no schedule is active, the app will follow the device’s system theme, ensuring consistency with user’s device settings.

This feature directly addresses user pain points and aligns with our goal to **reduce theme-related support tickets by 40% within one quarter of launch**. By automating theme transitions, we reduce cognitive load and improve user comfort during night shifts—leading to better usability and reduced support burden.

---

## **2. Problem Statement**

Night-shift nurses use Ledgerly to access clinical notes during early morning hours (2am–6am). Currently, the app only supports a manual light/dark toggle, which requires users to switch themes repeatedly in low-light environments. This leads to:

- Eye strain and discomfort during prolonged reading  
- Increased cognitive load from managing theme settings  
- A spike in support tickets related to theme issues (e.g., "Why is the app light when I want dark?")  
- Inconsistent user experience across devices and time-of-day  

This problem is both frequent and impactful, with user interviews indicating that 78% of night-shift nurses have experienced eye strain during note reading, and 65% have reported needing to manually toggle the theme multiple times per shift.

---

## **3. Goals & Objectives**

| Goal | Objective |
|------|-----------|
| **Reduce theme-related support tickets** | Cut theme-related support tickets by **40%** within one quarter of launch (Q2 2025) |
| **Improve user comfort** | Reduce eye strain during night shifts by providing a consistent, optimized theme experience |
| **Simplify user workflow** | Eliminate the need for manual theme toggling during night shifts |
| **Ensure accessibility compliance** | Respect reduce-motion and high-contrast settings at all times |

---

## **4. Target Users**

| User Type | Role | Key Needs |
|---------|------|----------|
| **Night-Shift Nurse** | Primary user | Reads clinical notes between 2am–6am; needs a dark, readable theme to reduce eye strain; uses device in low-light environments |
| **Shift Supervisor** | Secondary user | May use Ledgerly for quick note checks; benefits from consistent theme experience |
| **App Users with Accessibility Needs** | All users | Must have full compatibility with reduce-motion and high-contrast settings |

---

## **5. User Stories & Requirements**

### **User Story 1: Set a Time-Based Theme Schedule**

> **As a night-shift nurse**,  
> I want to set a schedule that turns the app to dark mode from 2am to 6am,  
> so that I can read notes comfortably without manually toggling the theme.

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- User can create a schedule with a start time and end time (e.g., 2:00 AM to 6:00 AM)  
- The app automatically switches to dark mode during the scheduled time  
- The app switches back to the system theme (or light mode) when outside the schedule  
- The app respects device system theme when no schedule is active  
- The app does not override user’s reduce-motion or high-contrast settings  

---

### **User Story 2: Set a Second Time-Based Theme Schedule**

> **As a night-shift nurse**,  
> I want to set a second schedule (e.g., 6am to 8am) for a different theme,  
> so that I can have a consistent theme during morning shifts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- Users can create a second schedule (e.g., 6:00 AM to 8:00 AM)  
- The app applies the correct theme during that window  
- Schedules are applied in order of time (earlier schedules take precedence)  
- Maximum of **two schedules** per account is enforced  

---

### **User Story 3: Default to System Theme**

> **As a user**,  
> I want the app to follow my device’s system theme when no schedule is active,  
> so that I can maintain consistency with my device settings.

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- When no schedule is set, the app uses the device’s system theme (light/dark)  
- This behavior is consistent across all devices and OS versions  
- The app does not override system theme settings  

---

### **User Story 4: Respect Accessibility Settings**

> **As a user**,  
> I want the app to respect my reduce-motion and high-contrast settings,  
> so that I can maintain my accessibility preferences.

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- The app does not apply animations or transitions when reduce-motion is enabled  
- The app respects high-contrast mode (e.g., text color, background contrast)  
- These settings are applied regardless of theme or schedule  
- Accessibility settings are not overridden by theme scheduling  

---

## **6. Success Metrics**

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Frequency |
|-------|--------|---------------------|----------|
| **Theme-related support tickets** | ↓ 40% from baseline | Support ticket logs (categorized by theme issues) | Weekly (Q2 2025) |
| **User satisfaction (eye strain)** | ↑ 20% | Post-usage survey (5-point scale: "How comfortable was reading notes?") | Bi-weekly (post-launch) |
| **Adoption rate of theme scheduler** | ≥ 70% of night-shift nurses | In-app usage analytics (schedule creation) | Monthly |
| **Average time to read a note** | ↓ 15% | Time-based analytics (from note open to close) | Monthly |
| **User engagement during night shifts** | ↑ 10% | App usage logs (active sessions between 2am–6am) | Weekly |

> **Baseline**: Current support ticket volume = 12 per week (Q1 2025)  
> **Target**: 7.2 tickets per week (40% reduction) by end of Q2 2025

---

## **7. Scope**

### **In-Scope**  
✅ Users can create up to **two time-based theme schedules**  
✅ App automatically applies the correct theme during scheduled times  
✅ App respects device system theme when no schedule is active  
✅ App respects **reduce-motion** and **high-contrast** accessibility settings  
✅ Schedules are applied in chronological order (earlier schedules take precedence)  
✅ Schedules are stored per user account  

### **Out-of-Scope**  
❌ Per-note themes (e.g., theme per note)  
❌ Syncing schedules across devices (e.g., phone ↔ tablet)  
❌ Theme scheduling for non-night-shift users  
❌ Theme-based notifications or alerts  
❌ Integration with third-party calendar apps  

---

## **8. Technical Considerations**

| Area | Details |
|------|--------|
| **Architecture** | Theme logic is handled in the app’s theme engine, which listens to system time and device settings |
| **Platform Support** | iOS and Android (both support system theme and accessibility settings) |
| **Accessibility** | Theme scheduler does not trigger animations; high-contrast mode is respected via OS-level settings |
| **Performance** | Theme switching is instantaneous (under 100ms); no noticeable lag during transitions |
| **Data Storage** | Schedules are stored in user account settings (local storage only; no cloud sync) |
| **Security** | No user data is stored or transmitted during theme scheduling |
| **Dependencies** | Requires access to device time, system theme, and accessibility settings APIs |

---

## **9. Design & UX Requirements**

- **UI Elements**  
  - "Theme Scheduler" section in Settings → Appearance  
  - Two editable time slots (start/end time) with clear labels  
  - Visual indicator showing current active schedule (e.g., "Dark mode active: 2am–6am")  
  - Toggle to "Use system theme" (default)  
  - Accessibility settings badge (e.g., "Reduce Motion: On")  

- **UX Flow**  
  1. User opens Settings → Appearance  
  2. Sees "Theme Scheduler" section  
  3. Can add or edit two time-based schedules  
  4. App automatically applies theme during active windows  
  5. App shows a subtle visual cue when theme changes (only if reduce-motion is off)  

- **Accessibility**  
  - All UI elements are labeled and keyboard-navigable  
  - High-contrast mode is respected in all views  
  - No animations when reduce-motion is enabled  

---

## **10. Timeline & Milestones**

| Phase | Timeline | Deliverables |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| **Discovery & Design** | Apr 5 – Apr 15 | User research, wireframes, accessibility review |
| **Development** | Apr 16 – May 15 | Theme scheduler logic, UI implementation |

# Product Requirements Document (PRD)  
**Feature**: Add Pagination to GET /orders Endpoint (REST API)  
**Product**: Kettleworks Public REST API  
**Version**: 1.0  
**Date**: April 5, 2025  

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Kettleworks’ public REST API is a critical component for third-party dashboard builders that rely on polling the `/orders` endpoint every minute to display real-time order data. Currently, when clients request more than 500 records, the API returns a timeout error, resulting in incomplete or missing data in dashboards. This leads to inaccurate analytics, user frustration, and loss of trust in Kettleworks as a reliable data source.

To resolve this, we are introducing **cursor-based pagination** to the GET `/orders` endpoint. This change will allow clients to retrieve large datasets efficiently without exceeding response time limits. The solution will maintain backward compatibility by preserving the existing `offset` parameter for one year, ensuring no disruption to current integrations.

The primary goal is to **keep the 95th percentile (p95) latency under 2 seconds for pages of 100 records**, a critical performance benchmark for real-time dashboard applications. This change is limited to **read-only endpoints** and does not introduce breaking changes to the response schema or data structure. No modifications are made to write endpoints, GraphQL, or webhooks.

This PRD outlines the requirements, user stories, success metrics, scope, and technical considerations for implementing this feature.

---

## 2. Problem Statement

Third-party dashboard builders poll the `/orders` endpoint every minute to display order data. When a request exceeds 500 records, the API times out due to memory and processing constraints. As a result:

- Clients receive incomplete or empty data.
- Dashboards show outdated or missing order information.
- Users lose confidence in the accuracy and reliability of Kettleworks data.
- Performance degradation impacts the user experience and adoption of Kettleworks in analytics tools.

This problem is especially acute for dashboards that aggregate large volumes of historical orders, where clients expect consistent, complete, and timely data.

---

## 3. Goals & Objectives

| Goal | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Primary Goal** | Achieve p95 latency < 2 seconds for pages of 100 records. |
| **Secondary Goal** | Maintain backward compatibility with the `offset` parameter for one year. |
| **Business Objective** | Improve data completeness and reliability for third-party dashboards, reducing support tickets and increasing user satisfaction. |
| **Technical Objective** | Implement efficient, scalable pagination without modifying the response schema or introducing breaking changes. |

---

## 4. Target Users

| User Type | Role | Needs |
|---------|------|-------|
| **Dashboard Builders** | Developers using tools like Tableau, Power BI, or custom dashboards | Reliable, complete, and timely access to order data. Must handle large datasets without timeouts. |
| **Data Analysts** | Internal or external analysts using Kettleworks data | Accurate, consistent, and complete order history for reporting. |
| **API Consumers** | Any application that polls `/orders` | Stable, predictable performance and data completeness. |

---

## 5. User Stories & Requirements

### User Story 1: Retrieve Orders Using Cursor-Based Pagination

**As a** dashboard builder,  
**I want to** retrieve orders using a cursor-based pagination scheme,  
**So that** I can efficiently fetch large datasets without timeouts or data loss.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The endpoint supports a new `cursor` query parameter.
- The `cursor` parameter is required for pagination.
- The response includes a `next_cursor` field with the next page’s cursor.
- The response includes a `has_more` field indicating whether there are more pages.
- The response body contains a list of orders (same structure as before).
- The API returns a 200 OK status for valid requests.
- The API returns a 400 error if `cursor` is malformed or missing.

---

### User Story 2: Continue Using Offset Parameter (Backward Compatibility)

**As a** dashboard builder using the existing `offset` parameter,  
**I want to** continue using the `offset` parameter for one year,  
**So that** I can maintain compatibility with current integrations without rework.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The `offset` parameter is supported and works as before.
- The `offset` parameter is valid for requests up to 500 records.
- For requests exceeding 500 records, the API returns a timeout error (not a 400 or 429).
- The `offset` parameter is **not** used for pagination beyond 500 records.
- The `offset` parameter is **not** supported for cursor-based pagination.
- The `offset` parameter will be deprecated in the next major version (v2.0) and removed in v3.0.

---

### User Story 3: Ensure p95 Latency < 2 Seconds for 100-Record Pages

**As a** dashboard builder,  
**I want** the API to respond within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile for a page of 100 records,  
**So that** my dashboard updates in real time without lag.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The p95 latency for a 100-record page is measured and confirmed to be under 2 seconds.
- Latency is measured using real-world load testing with 100+ concurrent requests.
- The test includes a variety of data volumes and order types.
- The test is repeated across multiple environments (dev, staging, prod).

---

### User Story 4: Maintain Read-Only Scope

**As a** product engineer,  
**I want** to ensure that only read-only operations are supported in this release,  
**So that** we avoid introducing write operations or data mutations.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- No write operations (e.g., `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) are added to the `/orders` endpoint.
- No new write endpoints are introduced.
- No changes to existing write endpoints are made.

---

## 6. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|-------|--------|---------------------|
| **p95 Latency** | < 2 seconds | Real-world load testing with 100-record pages and 100+ concurrent requests. |
| **Data Completeness** | 100% of records returned | Compare response size and record count against expected data volume. |
| **Timeout Rate** | 0% for requests ≤ 500 records | Monitor error logs for 408 (timeout) on requests with `offset` ≤ 500. |
| **Client Adoption** | 80% of dashboards using `/orders` adopt cursor-based pagination within 6 months | Track usage via API client logs and dashboard metadata. |
| **Support Tickets** | Reduce by 30% in 3 months | Monitor support tickets related to missing or incomplete order data. |

> **Note**: The p95 latency metric is aligned with the performance goal and is critical for real-time dashboards.

---

## 7. Scope

### ✅ In-Scope (This Release)

- Add **cursor-based pagination** to the GET `/orders` endpoint.
- Support the **`cursor`** parameter for pagination.
- Maintain the **`offset`** parameter for one year (until v2.0).
- Ensure **p95 latency < 2 seconds** for 100-record pages.
- Keep the **response schema unchanged** (no breaking changes).
- Limit changes to **read-only endpoints**.
- Support **read-only** operations only.

### ❌ Out-of-Scope

- **Write endpoints** (e.g., `POST /orders`, `PUT /orders`, `DELETE /orders`) — no changes.
- **GraphQL API** — no changes or additions.
- **Webhooks** — no changes or additions.
- **Future enhancements** (e.g., filtering, sorting, search) — deferred to v2.0.
- **Performance improvements beyond 100 records** — deferred to future releases.
- **Adding new fields or modifying response structure** — strictly prohibited.

---

## 8. Technical Considerations

### Architecture

- The `/orders` endpoint will use **cursor-based pagination** to avoid the inefficiency of offset-based pagination.
- The cursor is a unique identifier (e.g., a UUID or timestamp-based hash) derived from the last order in a page.
- The API will maintain a **monotonic order** of orders (by timestamp) to ensure consistent results.
- The response includes:
  - `orders`: array of order objects (same schema as before)
  - `next_cursor`: string (next page cursor)
  - `has_more`: boolean (true if more pages exist)

### Dependencies

- **No external dependencies** beyond existing database and query engine.
- The database must support efficient range queries by timestamp.
- The API layer must implement efficient cursor lookup and pagination logic.

### Security

- No new authentication or authorization requirements.
- Existing API key and rate-limiting mechanisms remain unchanged.
- All data is read-only — no mutations or side effects.

# **Product Requirements Document (PRD)**  
**Feature: Usage-Based Billing for Team Plan**  
**Product:** Ledgerly  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** April 5, 2025  

---

## **1. Executive Summary**

Ledgerly currently offers a flat monthly fee for its team plans, which is not aligned with actual usage by small agencies. These agencies—typically with 5 to 25 team members—store documents in the platform, and finance currently reconciles usage manually via spreadsheets, taking three days per month to complete. This process is error-prone, time-consuming, and lacks real-time visibility into costs.

To improve financial accuracy, reduce manual overhead, and increase transparency, we are introducing **usage-based billing** for team plans. This feature will automatically count stored documents nightly, project a live bill in real time, and generate invoices that list usage in **GB-months**. The goal is to convert **30% of flat-fee teams** to usage billing within **two quarters** (6 months), with all pricing in USD and monthly billing cycles only.

This change supports better cost visibility for small agencies, enables more accurate financial planning, and aligns pricing with actual platform consumption—driving adoption and trust in Ledgerly’s pricing model.

---

## **2. Problem Statement**

Small agencies using Ledgerly’s team plans currently pay a flat monthly fee regardless of how much data they store. This creates a disconnect between actual usage and cost, leading to:

- Manual reconciliation of usage by finance teams (3 days/month)
- Inaccurate cost tracking and budgeting
- Poor visibility into cost drivers
- Underutilization of platform capacity (some teams store far more than others)

This inefficiency results in financial misalignment and reduces trust in the product’s pricing model.

---

## **3. Goals & Objectives**

| Goal | Objective |
|------|-----------|
| **Improve financial accuracy** | Replace manual spreadsheet reconciliation with automated, real-time usage tracking |
| **Increase transparency** | Provide teams with a live projected bill in admin settings |
| **Drive adoption** | Convert 30% of flat-fee teams to usage billing within two quarters |
| **Enable cost-based pricing** | Align pricing with actual data consumption (in GB-months) |

---

## **4. Target Users**

- **Primary Users**:  
  - Small agencies (5–25 employees)  
  - Teams that store 100+ documents monthly, with average document size of 1–10 MB  
  - Finance or operations staff responsible for budgeting and cost tracking  

- **Secondary Users**:  
  - Admins who manage team plans and view usage metrics  
  - Product and sales teams monitoring adoption  

---

## **5. User Stories & Requirements**

### **User Story 1: Admin sees live projected bill**

**As a team admin,**  
**I want to see a live projected monthly bill in the admin settings,**  
**So that I can understand current and future costs without manual reconciliation.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- The projected bill is updated nightly and visible in the "Billing" section of the admin dashboard  
- The projected bill shows total cost in USD, based on current usage  
- The projected bill updates in real time (within 1 minute of the nightly run)  
- The projected bill is accurate to within ±5% of actual usage  

---

### **User Story 2: Usage is tracked in GB-months**

**As a team admin,**  
**I want to see usage in GB-months,**  
**So that I can understand how much data my team is consuming.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- Usage is calculated as **GB-months** (e.g., 100 documents × 5 MB = 0.5 GB × 1 month = 0.5 GB-month)  
- The calculation is consistent across all documents and stored files  
- The metric is displayed in the admin dashboard and in invoices  
- The calculation is based on actual stored file size and duration (from creation to deletion)  

---

### **User Story 3: Invoices list usage in GB-months**

**As a finance team member,**  
**I want to see usage in GB-months on invoices,**  
**So that I can reconcile costs with actual data consumption.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- Each invoice includes a line item: "Usage (GB-months)"  
- The usage value is derived from nightly calculations  
- The invoice shows total cost = base fee + (usage × rate per GB-month)  
- The rate per GB-month is fixed at $0.001 (1 cent per GB-month)  

---

### **User Story 4: Nightly usage calculation**

**As a backend system,**  
**I want to count stored documents nightly,**  
**So that usage data is accurate and available for billing.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- A nightly job runs at 2:00 AM UTC to calculate total stored data (in GB)  
- The job runs only for active team plans (not individual users)  
- The job runs in a non-blocking way (does not impact performance)  
- The result is stored in a database and used to generate the projected bill  

---

### **User Story 5: Usage data is available in admin settings**

**As a team admin,**  
**I want to see a breakdown of usage (GB-months) in the admin dashboard,**  
**So that I can monitor team data consumption.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- The dashboard shows:  
  - Total stored data (in GB)  
  - Total usage (in GB-months)  
  - Projected monthly cost

# **Product Requirements Document (PRD)**  
**Feature: Simplified Onboarding Flow for First-Time Users**  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** April 5, 2025  
**Owner:** Product Team – Onboarding & Growth  

---

## **1. Executive Summary**

Streakmill is a habit-building app that helps users build and maintain daily routines through streaks. Currently, our onboarding flow spans 11 screens and drops half of new users before they create their first habit—resulting in a day-7 retention rate of only 18%. This PRD outlines a redesigned onboarding flow that reduces friction, accelerates user engagement, and improves retention.

The new onboarding flow is designed specifically for adults who discover Streakmill through a friend’s streak screenshot. These users are motivated by social proof and are likely to act quickly after seeing a visual success story. The goal is to **raise day-7 retention from 18% to 25%** by streamlining the experience and eliminating unnecessary steps.

Key improvements:
- Reduced from 11 screens to **5 screens or fewer**
- Collects **one habit** and **one reminder time** (e.g., morning, evening)
- **Skips account creation** until the user completes the onboarding flow
- No email verification during onboarding
- English-only in this release
- Excludes social invites, referral codes, and habit imports

This flow prioritizes speed, simplicity, and immediate value—ensuring users feel successful and engaged from the very first interaction.

---

## **2. Problem Statement**

First-time users are dropping off early in the onboarding process. The current 11-screen flow requires users to:
- Create an account
- Enter email and password
- Navigate through multiple screens to select a habit
- Set a reminder time

This process is lengthy, intimidating, and feels like a "formal" experience rather than a joyful, personal one. As a result, **half of new users abandon the app before creating their first habit**, and day-7 retention remains at just 18%.

For users who see a friend’s streak screenshot, this friction is especially damaging—these users are already motivated by social proof and expect a quick, intuitive path to start using the app.

---

## **3. Goals & Objectives**

| Goal | Target |
|------|--------|
| Improve day-7 retention | From 18% → 25% |
| Reduce onboarding drop-off | From 50% → <30% |
| Increase habit creation completion | From 30% → 60% |
| Deliver immediate user value | Users complete a habit within 30 seconds of starting |

---

## **4. Target Users**

- **Primary User**: Adults aged 18–45 who download Streakmill after seeing a friend’s streak screenshot on social media or messaging apps.
- **User Motivation**: Inspired by social proof; wants to build a personal habit quickly and see visible progress.
- **Behavior**: Values simplicity, speed, and immediate results. Prefers minimal input and clear, visual feedback.

---

## **5. User Stories & Requirements**

### **User Story 1: As a first-time user, I want to start with one habit immediately so I can begin building my streak.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- User selects one habit from a curated list (e.g., "Drink water," "Walk 10 minutes," "Read 10 pages")
- Habit is saved and visible in the app after onboarding
- Habit appears in the daily streak dashboard on Day 1

---

### **User Story 2: As a first-time user, I want to set a reminder time so I don’t forget to complete my habit.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- User selects a reminder time from a list: "Morning (7–8 AM)", "Afternoon (12–1 PM)", "Evening (6–7 PM)"
- Reminder time is saved and triggers a notification at the selected time
- Notification appears only if the user has enabled notifications (default: on)

---

### **User Story 3: As a first-time user, I want to skip account creation until I finish the onboarding flow so I don’t feel overwhelmed.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- No account creation screens appear during onboarding
- User is not asked for email, password, or phone number
- After completing the habit and reminder, user is prompted to "Start your streak" with a simple "Yes" button
- Upon clicking "Yes," the user is taken to the home screen with their first habit and a welcome message

---

### **User Story 4: As a first-time user, I want to see a clear visual of what a streak looks like so I understand the value.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Onboarding includes a short animated or illustrated walkthrough of a streak (e.g., "You’ll see a growing line of dots—each day you complete your habit")
- The animation is shown only once and is non-intrusive
- The animation is accessible and shown in a mobile-friendly format

---

## **6. Success Metrics**

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|-------|--------|-------------------|
| Day-7 retention | ≥25% | Track % of users who open the app on Day 7 after first use |
| Habit creation completion | ≥60% | % of users who complete at least one habit after onboarding |
| Onboarding drop-off rate | ≤30% | % of users who exit before completing the flow |
| Time to first habit | ≤30 seconds | Average time from entry to habit selection |
| User satisfaction (post-onboarding) | ≥4.0/5.0 | Post-onboarding survey (NPS-style) |

> **Framework**: AARRR (Acquisition → Activation)  
> - **Activation**: Users complete a habit and set a reminder  
> - **Retention**: Day-7 retention is measured as a key success indicator  

---

## **7. Scope**

### **In-Scope**
- 5 screens or fewer in the onboarding flow  
- Collect one habit (from a curated list)  
- Collect one reminder time (from a list of 3 options)  
- Skip account creation until user completes onboarding  
- No email verification during onboarding  
- English-only language in this release  
- Onboarding flow is fully visual and minimal  

### **Out-of-Scope**
- Social invites or referral codes  
- Importing habits from other apps  
- Multi-language support (future release)  
- Account recovery or password reset during onboarding  
- Sharing habits publicly or with friends  
- Analytics or reporting during onboarding  

> *Note: All out-of-scope items are deferred to v2.0 or beyond.*

---

## **8. Technical Considerations**

- **Architecture**: Onboarding flow is a standalone flow in the app, triggered by a "Start Streak" button after a friend’s screenshot is shared.
- **Dependencies**:  
  - Habit list data stored in a static JSON file (pre-loaded)  
  - Reminder time options stored in app configuration  
  - No backend API calls during onboarding  
- **Security**:  
  - No personal data collected during onboarding  
  - No email or phone number stored  
- **Performance**:  
  - Onboarding flow must load in under 2 seconds  
  - All screens are lightweight and optimized for mobile  
- **Accessibility**:  
  - All text is large and readable  
  - Supports screen readers  
  - High-contrast mode available  
- **Data**:  
  - Habit and reminder data stored locally in user profile (no cloud sync until Day 14)  
  - No user ID or profile creation until post-onboarding  

---

## **9. Design & UX Requirements**

- **Visual Design**:  
  - Clean, modern, and playful aesthetic  
  - Uses Streakmill’s brand colors (blue, white, soft green)  
  - Icons and animations are simple and intuitive  
- **Interaction Patterns**:  
  - Each screen has a clear "Next" or "Continue" button  
  - Flow is linear and non-branching  
  - No modals or pop-ups during onboarding  
- **Accessibility**:  
  - WCAG 2.1 AA compliance (contrast, text size, navigation)  
  - Voiceover support for screen readers  
- **Responsive Design**:  
  - Optimized for mobile (iPhone and Android)  
  - No horizontal scrolling or complex layouts  

---

## **10. Timeline & Milestones**

| Phase | Duration | Deliverable |
|-------|---------|------------|
| Discovery & Design | Week 1 | Finalize habit list, flow wireframes, user testing plan |
| Prototype & Test | Week 2 | Interactive prototype tested with 10 users |
| Development | Week 3–4 | Build onboarding flow, integrate habit & reminder logic |
| QA & Testing | Week 5 | Test for usability, performance, and edge cases |
| Launch | Week 6 | Release to production with A/B test (vs. current flow) |
| Post-Launch Review | Week 7 | Analyze day-7 retention and adjust if needed |

> **Milestone**: Launch onboarding flow to 10% of new users (A/B test) by Week 6.

---

## **11. Risks & Mitigation**

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Users skip the flow and go to home screen | Add a subtle "Start your streak" CTA in the app’s splash screen after launch |
| Habit list is too generic | Curate list with real-life, relatable habits (e.g., "Drink water," "Stretch," "Read") |

# Product Requirements Document (PRD)  
**Feature: Inline Comments on Shared Dashboards**  
**Product:** Kettleworks  
**Date:** April 5, 2025  
**Owner:** Product Team – Analytics Experience  

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Marketing analysts at Kettleworks frequently collaborate on campaign reports by reviewing shared dashboards. Currently, feedback is captured in a separate spreadsheet, leading to confusion about which chart a comment refers to and making it difficult to track discussion context. This results in inefficiencies, misaligned insights, and lost follow-up.

To solve this, we are introducing **inline comments** directly within shared dashboards. These comments will allow analysts to anchor feedback to specific charts, reply in a thread, and resolve comments—ensuring that every piece of feedback is clearly tied to the data it refers to.

This feature will improve collaboration, reduce ambiguity, and increase the speed at which insights are shared and acted upon. We aim to achieve **60% of shared dashboards with at least one comment within 90 days** of launch.

The comments will be visible only within the workspace (private, not public), and will support only one level of replies—ensuring clarity and reducing complexity. Features like mentions, emoji reactions, and guest commenting are intentionally excluded to maintain focus and usability.

---

## 2. Problem Statement

Marketing analysts currently rely on a shared spreadsheet to provide feedback on campaign dashboards. This process leads to:

- **Ambiguity**: Comments are not linked to specific charts or data points, making it hard to know what they refer to.
- **Information loss**: When feedback is scattered across multiple sheets, it’s easy to lose track of context.
- **Delayed follow-up**: Without clear ownership or visibility, insights go unacted upon.
- **Reduced collaboration efficiency**: Time is spent searching for relevant notes instead of analyzing data.

This creates friction in the decision-making process and undermines the value of shared dashboards.

---

## 3. Goals & Objectives

| Goal | Objective |
|------|-----------|
| Improve collaboration efficiency | Enable analysts to provide and respond to feedback directly in dashboards |
| Reduce ambiguity in feedback | Anchor comments to specific charts and data points |
| Increase adoption of shared dashboards | Achieve 60% of shared dashboards with at least one comment within 90 days |
| Enhance insight actionability | Allow comments to be resolved, signaling when feedback has been addressed |

---

## 4. Target Users

- **Primary**: Marketing Analysts  
  - Use dashboards to evaluate campaign performance  
  - Collaborate with peers to validate insights and recommendations  
  - Need to provide and respond to feedback in real time  

- **Secondary**: Campaign Managers  
  - Review dashboards to make strategic decisions  
  - May use comments to request clarification or action items  

---

## 5. User Personas

| Persona | Role | Needs |
|--------|------|-------|
| **Alex Rivera** | Senior Marketing Analyst | Needs to quickly validate data points with peers and track discussion threads. Currently spends 15+ minutes per dashboard reviewing spreadsheets. |
| **Jamie Chen** | Junior Analyst | Needs to learn how to give feedback effectively. Seeks clear, visible feedback to avoid missing key insights. |

---

## 6. User Stories & Requirements

### User Story 1: Anchor a Comment to a Chart

**As a marketing analyst,**  
**I want to add a comment to a specific chart in a shared dashboard,**  
**so that I can clearly reference which data point or insight I’m discussing.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- A comment can be added by clicking a "Comment" button on any chart (e.g., a bar chart, line graph).  
- The comment appears inline, directly beneath the chart.  
- The comment is anchored to the specific chart and data point (e.g., "Q3 revenue" on a bar chart).  
- The comment is visible only within the workspace and not shared publicly.  

---

### User Story 2: Reply in a Thread

**As a marketing analyst,**  
**I want to reply to a comment in a thread,**  
**so that I can discuss follow-up questions or clarify points.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- After a comment is posted, a "Reply" button appears below it.  
- Replies appear in a thread below the original comment.  
- The thread is limited to **one level of replies** (no nested replies).  
- Replies are visible only within the workspace.  
- The thread is clearly labeled with "Replies" and shows the user who posted each message.  

---

### User Story 3: Resolve a Comment

**As a marketing analyst,**  
**I want to mark a comment as resolved,**  
**so that I know the feedback has been addressed and no further action is needed.**

**Acceptance Criteria:**  
- A "Mark as Resolved" button appears when a comment has been replied to or acted upon.  
- Once resolved, the comment status changes to "Resolved" and is no longer editable.  
- The resolution is visible to all users in the workspace.  
- Resolved comments are still visible but are marked clearly (e.g., with a checkmark icon).  

---

## 7. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Frequency |
|-------|--------|---------------------|----------|
| **Dashboard comment adoption rate** | ≥60% of shared dashboards have at least one comment within 90 days | Count of dashboards with comments / Total shared dashboards | Weekly |
| **Average time to respond to a comment** | ≤24 hours | Track time from comment creation to first reply | Monthly |
| **Comment resolution rate** | ≥70% of comments are resolved within 7 days | Count of resolved comments / Total comments | Weekly |
| **User satisfaction (NPS)** | ≥70 | Post-implementation survey (post-use feedback) | Post-launch (30 days) |

> **Note**: The "North Star Metric" for this feature is **comment adoption rate**, as it directly reflects how effectively the feature is being used and integrated into daily workflows.

---

## 8. Scope

### ✅ In-Scope  
- Anchor comments to specific charts or data points  
- Allow users to reply in a thread (one level deep)  
- Enable resolution of comments  
- Comments visible only within the workspace (private)  
- Support for shared dashboards only (not public dashboards)  

### ❌ Out-of-Scope  
- Mentions (e.g., "@user")  
- Emoji reactions (e.g., 👍, ❤️)  
- Guest commenting (only authenticated users can comment)  
- Nested replies (only one level of replies)  
- Comment visibility outside the workspace  
- Comment history or audit trail  
- Integration with external tools (e.g., Slack, email)  

> *Note: Out-of-scope items are intentional to maintain simplicity and reduce cognitive load. Future iterations can expand these features.*

---

## 9. Technical Considerations

- **Architecture**:  
  - Comments are stored as lightweight, inline objects within the dashboard data model.  
  - Each comment is tied to a chart via a unique identifier (e.g., chart ID + data point).  
  - Data is stored in the Kettleworks backend with a private workspace scope.

- **Dependencies**:  
  - Existing dashboard rendering engine must support inline UI elements.  
  - Authentication system must ensure only workspace members can view and comment.  
  - No external APIs required.

- **Security & Privacy**:  
  - All comments are stored within the workspace and are not accessible to external users or public views.  
  - Data is encrypted at rest and in transit.  
  - No personal data is collected.

- **Performance**:  
  - Comment loading should not impact dashboard rendering time.  
  - Maximum comment count per chart: 10 (to prevent clutter).  
  - Load time for dashboards with comments: <1 second.

- **Compatibility**:  
  - Works on all Kettleworks browser and mobile views.  
  - Responsive design ensures comments are visible on all screen sizes.

---

## 10. Design & UX Requirements

- **Visual Design**:  
  - Comment box appears as a small, clean card beneath each chart.  
  - Default comment field is labeled "Add a comment..." with a placeholder: "e.g., 'This trend seems off—did we miss a data point?'"  
  - When a comment is posted, it appears with a user avatar and timestamp.  
  - Replies appear in a thread below the original comment, with a "Replies" header and user name/time.

- **Interaction Patterns**:  
  - Click "Comment" → text input appears → submit → comment appears.  
  - Click "Reply" → new input field appears → submit → reply appears.  
  - Click "Mark as Resolved" → status changes to "Resolved" with a checkmark icon.  

- **Accessibility**:  
  - All comments are keyboard-navigable.  
  - Supports screen reader announcements.  
  - Text contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA standards.  

- **Design System Components**:  
  - Uses Kettleworks’ design tokens for colors, fonts, and spacing.  
  - Comment UI follows the "Kettleworks Feedback Pattern" (existing pattern for feedback in reports).

---

## 11. Timeline & Milestones

| Phase | Timeline | Deliverables |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| **Discovery & Design** | Day 1–10 | User research, wireframes, design system alignment |
| **Development** | Day 11–45 | Backend API, frontend implementation, testing |
| **QA & UAT** | Day 46–55 | Bug fixes, usability

# **Product Requirements Document (PRD)** **Feature: Full-Text Search in Ledgerly Notes** --- ## **1. Executive Summary** Ledgerly researchers maintain thousands of notes—often exceeding 2,000—across diverse topics, projects, and timelines. Currently, the search functionality only matches note *titles*, leading to significant inefficiency. Users report spending minutes scrolling through hundreds of results to locate a single paragraph they half-remember. This creates a friction point that undermines productivity and user satisfaction. This PRD outlines the implementation of **full-text search** across note *body text* to solve this problem. The new search will return results in under **2 seconds** for the largest accounts (e.g., enterprise users with 2,000+ notes), support **phrase queries**, **filter by tag and date**, and **highlight matched terms** in results—all without relying on external search services. The solution is built entirely on Ledgerly’s own servers using in-house text indexing, ensuring data privacy, control, and performance. This feature directly supports researchers’ core workflow by enabling rapid retrieval of content, reducing cognitive load, and improving time-to-insight. --- ## **2. Problem Statement** Researchers at Ledgerly maintain extensive note collections—often over 2,000 notes—covering research, ideas, and project planning. These notes are stored in plain text and are not indexed beyond titles. Currently, search only matches note titles. When users attempt to find a specific idea or paragraph, they must manually scroll through hundreds of results, often with no indication of relevance. This results in: - Significant time loss (average 3–5 minutes per search) - Increased frustration and cognitive load - Reduced trust in the product as a reliable research tool This inefficiency directly contradicts the goal of enabling fast, intuitive access to knowledge—core to the researcher experience. --- ## **3. Goals & Objectives** | Goal | Description | |------|-------------| | **Primary Goal** | Enable researchers to find relevant note content within seconds, reducing search time from minutes to under 2 seconds for the largest accounts. | | **Secondary Goals** | - Support phrase queries (e.g., "machine learning model") to improve precision.
- Allow filtering by tag and date to refine results.
- Highlight matched terms in search results to improve readability and relevance. | | **Business Objective** | Improve researcher productivity and satisfaction, leading to increased retention and adoption of Ledgerly as a core research tool. | --- ## **4. Target Users** | User Type | Characteristics | |---------|----------------| | **Primary User** | Researchers with 2,000+ notes who frequently search for specific ideas, concepts, or references. They rely on notes as a primary knowledge base. | | **Secondary User** | Project managers and team leads who use notes to track ideas and decisions. | **User Pain Points:** - Cannot find a specific idea or paragraph without scrolling through hundreds of results. - Search results are not relevant or prioritized. - No ability to filter by tags or date to narrow down results. - No visual indication of what was matched in a result. --- ## **5. User Stories & Requirements** ### **User Story 1: Search by Full-Text Content** > **As a researcher**, > I want to search for a specific idea or paragraph in the body of my notes, > so that I can quickly find relevant content without scrolling through hundreds of title-only matches. **Acceptance Criteria:** - Search results return full-text matches from note body content. - Results are returned in under 2 seconds for accounts with 2,000+ notes. - Search is case-insensitive and supports partial matches. - Search results are sorted by relevance (based on match score). --- ### **User Story 2: Phrase Query Support** > **As a researcher**, > I want to search for a phrase (e.g., "machine learning model") to find notes that contain that exact sequence, > so that I can find specific technical concepts or ideas without false positives. **Acceptance Criteria:** - Phrase queries are supported (e.g., "machine learning model" matches only if the full phrase appears). - The search engine treats phrases as a single unit (not split by spaces). - Results are clearly labeled with "Phrase Match" indicator. --- ### **User Story 3: Filter by Tag** > **As a researcher**, > I want to filter search results by tag (e.g., "AI", "research", "project"), > so that I can narrow down results to only those relevant to my current work. **Acceptance Criteria:** - Tags are extracted from note metadata and used in search filtering. - Filter options are available in the search UI (dropdown or sidebar). - Filtering updates results in real-time. --- ### **User Story 4: Filter by Date Range** > **As a researcher**, > I want to filter search results by date range (e.g., "last 30 days"), > so that I can find recent notes or track evolving ideas over time. **Acceptance Criteria:** - Date filtering is available in the search UI (e.g., "Created After", "Created Before"). - Date range is applied to note creation date. - Results update in real-time as filters are adjusted. --- ### **User Story 5: Highlight Matched Terms** > **As a researcher**, > I want to see highlighted text in search results to know which parts of the note were matched, > so that I can quickly assess relevance without reading the full note. **Acceptance Criteria:** - Matched terms (e.g., "machine learning") are visually highlighted in the result snippet. - Highlighting is consistent with the original note formatting (e.g., bold, color). - Highlighting is applied to both single terms and phrases. --- ## **6. Success Metrics** | Metric | Target | Measurement Method | |-------|--------|-------------------| | **Search Response Time** | < 2 seconds for accounts with 2,000+ notes | Latency measured from search input to first result render (frontend) | | **Search Accuracy** | 85%+ of results are relevant to the query | A/B test with researchers: % of users who find what they were looking for | | **Phrase Query Precision** | 90%+ of results contain the exact phrase | Test with 100+ queries; % of results that contain the full phrase | | **User Satisfaction** | 4.5/5 average rating on post-search survey | Post-search survey (N=100+ users) | | **Search Adoption Rate** | 70%+ of active users perform at least one full-text search per week | Analytics on search frequency and usage patterns | > **North Star Metric**: *Time saved per search* — measured as minutes saved compared to title-only search (based on user-reported search time). --- ## **7. Scope** ### ✅ **In-Scope** - Full-text search across note body content (text only) - Phrase query support (exact phrase matching) - Filter by tag and date - Highlighting of matched terms in results - Search performance optimized to return first page in <2 seconds for largest accounts - All indexing and search logic runs on Ledgerly’s own servers (no external services) ### ❌ **Out-of-Scope** - Saved searches (users cannot save or reuse search queries) - Search alerts (e.g., email notifications when new results appear) - OCR of image-based notes (only text content is indexed) - Search history or query logging (for privacy and performance reasons) > *Note: This scope ensures minimal impact on existing architecture and avoids introducing new dependencies.* --- ## **8. Technical Considerations** ### **Architecture Overview** - **Text Indexing**: Use a lightweight, in-memory text indexing engine (e.g., **Trie + Inverted Index**) to store and search note body text. - **Indexing Strategy**: - Notes are indexed on write (when a note is created or updated). - Index is updated incrementally (no full reindexing on every change). - Index is stored in a persistent, optimized format (e.g., SQLite or custom binary format). - **Search Engine**: Built from scratch using a custom search engine with: - Tokenization (splitting text into words/phrases) - Inverted index (mapping terms to note IDs) - Phrase matching (using n-gram or exact string matching) - **Performance Optimization**: - Caching of frequently accessed note bodies and indexes. - Query optimization (e.g., early filtering by tag/date before full text search). - Use of efficient data structures (e.g., Bloom filters for fast pre-filtering). ### **Dependencies** - **No external services** (search, AI, or cloud APIs). - Requires access to note body text (already stored in database). - Must support real-time updates to index (as notes are created/edited). ### **Security & Privacy** - All text indexing and search occurs on Ledgerly’s servers. - No data is sent to external services. - Search results are returned only to authenticated users. - No personal or sensitive data is indexed beyond note content. ### **Performance Constraints** - Must return **first page of results in under 2 seconds** for accounts with 2,000+ notes. - First page = top 10–20 results (based on relevance). - Performance is measured under peak load (e.g., 100+ concurrent searches). --- ## **9. Design & UX Requirements** ### **UI/UX Elements** - Search bar at the top of the notes list or in a dedicated panel. - Search input supports: - Real-time autocomplete (optional, future iteration) - Phrase query
